Byzantine emperor from 1425 to 1448, the eldest son of Manuel II. He ruled little more than Constantinople and a few towns, while the Ottomans under Murad II closed in.

His one real hope was help from the Catholic West, and the price was church union. In 1437 he sailed to Italy with the patriarch and a large Greek delegation. At the Council of Florence in 1439 they signed a union with Rome. Most Greeks at home rejected it, and the help it bought ended in disaster at the Battle of Varna in 1444.

While in Italy he sat for the artist Pisanello, whose bronze medal of the emperor in his tall hat is one of the best known images of a Byzantine ruler. He died childless, and his brother Constantine XI took the throne.
sum: Byzantine emperor from 1425 to 1448, the eldest son of Manuel II. He ruled little more than Constantinople and a few towns, while the Ottomans under Murad II closed in.
